name: Exodus

objectives.text: Identify Exodus as the book of the Bible that tells how God brought Israel out of slavery in Egypt
Retell how God protected baby Moses in a basket on the Nile River
Name Moses as the leader God called at the burning bush to bring Israel out of Egypt
Recall how God parted the Red Sea so Israel could cross on dry ground
Describe how God provided manna, quail, and water for Israel in the wilderness before Sinai
Recite the Ten Commandments in order as God gave them at Mount Sinai
Summarize the ten plagues and explain how they showed God's power over Pharaoh and the gods of Egypt
Explain the meaning of the word exodus as a going out and show how the title fits the book
Explain what God commanded Israel to do at the first Passover and why the blood on the doorposts spared their firstborn
Explain how God's covenant promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob are the reason Exodus gives for the rescue from Egypt
Explain why the Ten Commandments begin by recalling God's rescue from Egypt before giving any command
Explain how the Song of the Sea praises the LORD as warrior and king after the crossing
Explain how the golden calf account shows Israel's idolatry, Moses' intercession, and God's mercy in renewing the covenant
Analyze the structure of Exodus in three movements of deliverance from Egypt, covenant at Sinai, and the building of the tabernacle
Explain the terms of the Sinai covenant, including Israel's calling to be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation and the ratifying blood ceremony
Interpret the divine name revealed at the burning bush and explain what it teaches about God's self-existence and covenant faithfulness
Analyze how the New Testament presents Christ as the fulfillment of the Passover lamb
Analyze how Exodus describes the hardening of Pharaoh's heart as both Pharaoh's own act and God's judicial act
Explain the purpose of the tabernacle as God's dwelling among his people and how its layout and furnishings expressed his holiness
Analyze how New Testament writers use tabernacle imagery to describe the person and work of Christ
Construct a map of the proposed routes of the Exodus and explain the textual and geographical clues behind each
Compare the laws of the Book of the Covenant with ancient Near Eastern law codes such as the Code of Hammurabi
Evaluate the biblical and archaeological arguments for the early and late dates of the Exodus
Evaluate minimalist claims against the historicity of the Exodus using textual and archaeological evidence
Compose an essay tracing how later Scripture uses the Exodus as a pattern of redemption for the return from exile and the work of Christ

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (title, Moses, Red Sea, plagues, Passover, structure, divine name, Passover lamb and Christ, tabernacle, routes map, dating, historicity, salvation paradigm essay). Dropped vague filler (observing commandments as rules, comparing slavery to freedom, applying the lesson that God rescues) or replaced them with assessable versions such as reciting the Decalogue and explaining the prologue. Added missing content: Moses' birth, wilderness provision before Sinai, Abrahamic covenant motive, Song of the Sea, golden calf and covenant renewal, Sinai covenant terms, hardening of Pharaoh, NT tabernacle imagery, and the Book of the Covenant compared with ANE law. Replaced WCF 8.4 with 8.5, which addresses Christ's sacrifice, and added catechism anchors for the Decalogue and divine name. Left sacrificial system, later wilderness wanderings, and law-gospel uses to sibling sub-topics.
